text:
Iris: quick flag 0: staging billing showed duplication when late events arrived after compact. low volume but reproduced reliably on heavy-stream tenants.
Noah: ok can you show the minimal event?
Iris: example: ```{ "tenant": "acme-7", "req_id": "r-77", "tokens": 9, "fp": "fp-77-xyz", "ingest_ts": 1690000000 }``` we dedupe upstream by fp+req.
Keiko: so compact created a snapshot and then late tail created another claim that the finalizer accepted?
Iris: yeah. finalizer has no strong tie-back to the compact proof so it treated the late arrival as new.
Ben: we've discussed slop vs finalizer authority. new angle: what if the compact emits a small "provenance receipt" per fingerprint that the finalizer can verify before accepting new credits? then late events without matching receipt are treated as repair candidates.
Noah: interesting. what's in a provenance receipt?
Ben: sketch: receipt = {window_id, fingerprint, compact_seq, proof_ref, sig}. compact writes receipts to proofs store and publishes a small index to `metering.receipts`. finalizer, on ingest of an event referencing a compacted window, checks receipts for fp; if match -> accept; if missing -> emit repair_voucher.
Keiko: repair_voucher?
Ben: voucher is an audit-first intent that contains enough proof pointers for a deterministic reconciliation. example voucher: ```{ "type": "repair_voucher", "tenant": "acme-7", "window": "2026-03-22T10:00Z", "fps": ["fp-77-xyz"], "compact_seq": 987, "proofs": ["s3://proofs/..."] }``` worker consumes vouchers and applies reconciled deltas. vouchers are idempotent and carry proof refs so support can trace.
Iris: this avoids a heavy scan in the finalizer and gives an auditable trail. good.
Noah: tradeoffs: we add another small stream and need to ensure receipts are written atomically with compaction. also compact must produce receipts for all dedupe keys we care about.
Keiko: cost: receipts index size ~ (#fingerprints per window) * small entry. we can shard receipts by tenant and window. TTL maybe 7d.
Ben: advantage: finalizer can enforce strong acceptance rule: if event references a compacted window and there's a matching receipt with equal or newer compact_seq, accept; else emit voucher instead of accepting blindly. reduces accidental duplicate credits.
Iris: what about long-running requests that started before compaction and only finish after? request_start window vs commit window conflict. receipts need to include request_start when available.
Noah: receipts could include request_anchor: request_id or start_window. finalizer uses anchor to decide whether to attach to existing claim or create voucher.
Keiko: operational flow for vouchers: (1) finalizer emits voucher to audit.vouchers; (2) voucher worker fetches proofs and raw events (if still available), computes canonical assignment, then calls finalizer.apply_repair(canonical_delta) which must be CAS-protected. (3) finalizer emits audit.repair_applied with delta.
Ben: ensure vouchers include customer-visible reason and proof links so we can surface in billing UI: e.g., "merged duplicate from late tail, delta -9 tokens".
Iris: retention: raw events 7d, receipts TTL 7d, proofs 30d. vouchers allowed to resolve within receipts TTL; beyond that resolution must rely solely on proofs and can be "best-effort" with manual review flag.
Noah: failure modes: if voucher worker can't reconcile due to missing raw events, it should mark voucher state=requires_review and surface a ticket. avoid silent no-ops.
Keiko: need to ensure ledger invariants: finalizer.apply_repair must perform a CAS on compact_seq and ledger_seq and produce monotonic audit events. we must not produce negative-credit races.
Ben: implement CAS contract: apply_repair(repair_id, expected_compact_seq, deltas) -> {status:applied|conflict|invalid, seq}. If conflict, worker re-fetch receipts and re-run canonicalization.
Iris: UI/alerting: surface voucher_count and voucher_resolution_latency per tenant; add threshold alert if >X unresolved vouchers. Also log repair deltas in billing feed with tag "auto-repair".
Noah: security: proofs and receipts must be signed or have access controls to prevent tampering. proofs stored in S3 with KMS. receipts stream should be append-only topic with ACLs.
Keiko: do we want customers to be able to request ad-hoc reconciliation? e.g., "reconcile window W" API that emits a voucher and forces worker to run on demand.
Ben: could be useful for enterprise customers. add rate limits and require justification. make it a paid support flow initially.
Iris: action items: (1) Ben to write receipt format and topic contract; (2) Keiko to draft voucher schema and worker behavior; (3) Noah to update finalizer CAS contract and security model; (4) Iris to prototype receipts in staging and measure index size.
Noah: timeline?
Ben: receipt prototype this week, voucher worker spike next week.
ops-bot: branch `metering-receipts-vouchers` created and CI started (:rocket:)
Iris: thanks all. receipts + vouchers gives us deterministic, auditable repairs while keeping slop small. we can iterate on TTLs after staging metrics.
